chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Recitation (of Quran) is disliked in the obligatory prayer, but in the voluntary prayer, there is no harm, by God.'
And that which indicates that the preferable option is to separate the two Tawafs with prayer, when one has the choice, is what has been narrated:
ai.seo_question: Is Quranic recitation required or disliked in obligatory prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the juristic distinction between obligatory and voluntary prayers regarding Quranic recitation, noting that while recitation is disliked in fard prayers, it is permissible in nafl. The text further links this to the ritual of Tawaf, indicating that separating the two circuits with a two-rak'ah prayer is the preferred (afdhal) practice when one has the choice, reflecting the Shia emphasis on following the Imams' specific ritual nuances.
